entries.definitionCN: 因数；因子；能整除另一数的数或式子

entries.definition: to write an expression as a product of factors
the act of splitting something into factors
entries.definitionCN: 因式分解；把式子或数拆成因子的过程

entries.definition: able to be divided exactly by a given number
entries.definitionCN: 可整除的；能被某数除尽的

entries.definition: able to be broken down into simpler parts
entries.definitionCN: 可分解的；能拆成更简单部分的

entries.definition: able to be made simpler or smaller

normalIntro.en: Factorable is factor plus -able: whatever can be turned into factors is factorable.
normalIntro.cn: factorable 就是 factor 加 -able：能化成因式的东西，就叫可分解的。

normal.en: Factor is the noun, -able says it can be done, so factorable means able to be factored.
normal.cn: factor 是名词，-able 表示「能够」，所以 factorable 就是能被分解成因式的。

normal.en: The Latin facere, to make, is the root of factor.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 facere（制造）是 factor 的根。

normal.en: In algebra, a factorable polynomial splits into brackets.
normal.cn: 在代数里，可分解的多项式会拆成几个括号相乘。

normal.en: In arithmetic, a factorable number splits into divisors.
normal.cn: 在算术里，可分解因数的数会拆成几个约数。

normal.en: Compare factional: it means of a faction, not able to be factored.
normal.cn: 对比 factional：它指派系的，与「可分解」无关。

abstract.en: Picture a long block of wood coming apart into three smaller blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一块长木条拆成三块小木块。

abstract.en: Imagine the same blocks sorted into two piles, one of whole numbers and one of fractions.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的木块被分成两堆，一堆是整数块，一堆是分数块。

abstract.en: Think of a chocolate bar breaking neatly along its scored lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一块巧克力沿着压痕整齐地掰开。

examples.en: The teacher asked which of the expressions were factorable.
examples.cn: 老师问这些式子里哪些是可因式分解的。

examples.en: A factorable number can be written as a product of smaller numbers.
examples.cn: 可分解因数的数能写成几个更小数的乘积。

examples.en: This quadratic is factorable over the integers.
examples.cn: 这个二次式在整数范围内可因式分解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近似「法克特若波」——把式子「分」开成几「块」，正好是可分解的样子；这只是谐音联想，不是词源考证。

root: 拉丁语 facere（做、制造）→ factor（做事者，后指相乘的因子）→ 英语加 -able → factorable，核心义「能被拆成因子的」。

sensesIntro.en: Factorable moves from algebraic factorization to factorization over a chosen number set, and then to whole numbers split into divisors.
sensesIntro.cn: factorable 从代数式的因式分解，走到指定数集内的分解，再到整数拆成约数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long block that comes apart into smaller blocks which still fit together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块长条积木拆成几块小块，仍能拼回原样。

branches.en: The algebraic sense is the core: an expression that splits into factors.
branches.cn: 代数义是核心：能拆成因式的式子。

branches.en: The restricted sense says in which number set the split is allowed.
branches.cn: 受限义说明允许在哪个数集里拆分。

branches.en: Whole numbers split into divisors rather than brackets.
branches.cn: 整数拆成的是约数，而不是括号。

branches.en: Both senses depend on the same operation, and only the allowed numbers differ.
branches.cn: 两个义项依赖同一操作，区别只在允许使用的数。

branches.en: A factorable expression and a factorable integer are both products in disguise.
branches.cn: 可分解的式子与可分解因数的整数，本质上都是伪装的乘积。

intro.en: Factorable is factor plus the suffix -able, a pattern English uses for what can be done to something.
intro.cn: factorable 是 factor 加后缀 -able，英语用这个模式表示「可以被……处理」。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, to do or make, gives factor, a doer; the suffix -able descends from Latin -abilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere（做、制造）给出 factor（做事者）；后缀 -able 源自拉丁语 -abilis。

items.example: Factor came into English from this noun.
items.exampleCN: factor 由这个名词进入英语。

items.example: Factor gains its math sense in English.
items.exampleCN: factor 在英语中获得数学含义。

items.example: Factorable applies to expressions and numbers.
items.exampleCN: factorable 用于描述式子与数。

items.example: Factorize is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: factorize 是这个词族的动词。

items.meaning: the process of splitting into factors
items.meaningCN: 因式分解；分解因数的过程

definition_zh: 事实的；真实的；据实的；客观的
definition_en: based on facts, or concerned with what is true and actual
core_image: 一只手指按在档案纸上，指着上面一行确凿的记录
scene: 编辑把稿子里的每个数字都对着原始记录核了一遍。The report is factual and cites every source.
sceneCN: 这里 factual 是「据实的、以事实为依据的」（第 1 个义项：建立在事实之上）；句意：这篇报道据实而写，每一处都注明了来源。

pos.zh: 事实的；真实的；据实的；客观的

derivatives.zh: 事实；拉丁语 factum（所做之事）进入英语后的名词
据实地；在事实层面上；factual 加 -ly 构成
据实性；factual 加 -ness 构成
事实性；factual 加 -ity 构成

senses.title: Based on facts
senses.titleCN: 以事实为依据的；据实的
senses.definition: built on or supported by facts
senses.definitionCN: 建立在事实之上或有事实支撑的
senses.example: The account is factual and avoids speculation.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇叙述据实而写，没有臆测。
senses.why: Factual joins fact to -ual, so it describes what rests on things that actually happened.
senses.whyCN: factual 由 fact 加 -ual 构成，因此描述「以真实发生之事为依据」的东西。

senses.title: True and actual
senses.definition: real and actually the case, not imagined or invented
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在、确有其事，而非想象或编造
senses.example: The novel mixes factual places with invented characters.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把真实存在的地点与虚构的人物混在一起。
senses.why: Fact in English came to mean a thing that is true, and the adjective took that sense of reality.
senses.whyCN: fact 在英语里逐渐指「真实之事」，形容词便承接了这层「真实」的含义。

senses.title: Objective, without interpretation
senses.definition: concerned with plain information rather than opinion or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 只陈述平实信息，不带观点或情绪
senses.example: A factual tone suits a weather bulletin better than a lyrical one.
senses.exampleCN: 天气预报用客观的语气，比抒情语气更合适。
senses.why: A statement of fact leaves judgement out, so factual came to mark a plain, uncoloured style.
senses.whyCN: 陈述事实不带判断，于是 factual 也用来标记平实、不加色彩的表达方式。

senses.title: Of a question of fact in law
senses.definition: in law, relating to what happened rather than to a rule of law
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，指关乎发生了什么而非法律规则本身的
senses.example: The court left the factual question to the jury.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把事实问题留给陪审团判断。
senses.why: Law separates what happened from what the law says, and factual names the first half of that pair.
senses.whyCN: 法律把「发生了什么」与「法律怎么规定」分开，factual 指前一半。

intro.en: Factual is fact plus -ual; fact goes back to Latin factum, a thing done, from facere, to do.
intro.cn: factual 是 fact 加 -ual；fact 可追到拉丁语 factum（所做之事），源于 facere（做）。

items.en: Facere means to do or make.
items.cn: facere 意为做、制造。

items.en: Factum, the neuter past participle, means a thing done or an event.
items.cn: factum 是中性过去分词，意为「所做之事」或「发生的事」。

items.en: English fact first means a deed or an act, and later a thing that is true.
items.cn: 英语 fact 先指行为、事迹，后来才指真实之事。

items.en: Factual is formed in the nineteenth century as the adjective of fact.
items.cn: factual 在十九世纪形成，作 fact 的形容词。

items.en: Modern English uses factual for reports, evidence, and questions of fact.
items.cn: 现代英语用 factual 描述报道、证据以及事实问题。

note.en: Factual is the adjective of fact, close in sense to actual, and easily confused with factious and fictitious.
note.cn: factual 是 fact 的形容词，意义接近 actual，也容易与 factious、fictitious 这类形近词混淆。

entries.definition: a thing that is known to be true
given to forming factions
entries.definitionCN: 好结党的；与 factual 拼写相近，但来自 factio（派系），意义不同

entries.definition: invented rather than real
entries.definitionCN: 虚构的；只是拼写相近，其来源是 fingere（捏造），与 factual 不同源

entries.definition: real and existing in fact
telling the truth
based on facts rather than feelings
entries.definitionCN: 客观的；基于事实而非感情的

normalIntro.en: Factual is fact plus -ual: fact is a thing done, and factual describes what stays with things done.
normalIntro.cn: factual 是 fact 加 -ual：fact 是「做成的事」，factual 则形容紧贴这些事实的东西。

normal.en: Fact is the noun; factual is the adjective that says something rests on facts.
normal.cn: fact 是名词，factual 是形容词，表示某事物以事实为依据。

normal.en: The Latin factum means a thing done, which is where fact begins.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 factum 意为「所做之事」，fact 正是从这里开始。

normal.en: A factual report gives names and figures, not opinions.
normal.cn: factual 的报道给的是名称与数据，而不是观点。

normal.en: Factual accuracy is what editors check before printing.
normal.cn: 付印之前，编辑核对的就是「factual accuracy」（事实准确性）。

normal.en: Compare actual: actual stresses that something exists, factual stresses that it rests on facts.
normal.cn: 对比 actual：actual 强调某事物确实存在，factual 强调它以事实为依据。

abstract.en: Picture a finger running down a column of dated entries in an archive.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着档案里一列记着日期的条目往下划。

abstract.en: Imagine a photograph taken on the spot instead of a painted scene.
abstract.cn: 想象一张现场拍下的照片，而不是画出来的场景。

abstract.en: Think of a page with adjectives and adverbs crossed out, leaving only plain statements.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上把形容词和副词都划掉，只剩平铺直叙的句子。

examples.en: The witness gave a factual account of the accident.
examples.cn: 证人对事故做了据实的叙述。

examples.en: Check the factual accuracy of every figure in the table.
examples.cn: 核对表格里每个数字的事实准确性。

examples.en: Their disagreement was factual, not personal.
examples.cn: 他们的分歧是事实层面的，不是针对个人的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「factual」读作「法克图尔」——先有做出来的事，才有摆得上桌面的「事实」；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 facere（做）→ factum（所做之事）→ 英语 fact（事实）→ 加 -ual → factual，核心义「以做过、发生过的事为凭」。

sensesIntro.en: Factual begins with what is based on facts, widens to what is real, then marks an objective style, and finally names a legal question of fact.
sensesIntro.cn: factual 从「以事实为依据」开始，扩展到「真实的」，再指客观平实的表达，最后指法律上的事实问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger on a line of the record, checking it against what happened.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指按在记录的一行上，与发生过的事逐字核对。

branches.en: What rests on facts is the first sense.
branches.cn: 以事实为依据，是第一义。

branches.en: Real rather than invented is the reality sense.
branches.cn: 真实而非虚构，是「真实」这一义。

branches.en: Plain style follows when judgement is left out.
branches.cn: 不带判断，便引出平实的表达风格。

branches.en: In law the same adjective marks a question of fact.
branches.cn: 在法律上，同一个形容词标记「事实问题」。

branches.en: Report, reality, and tone all keep the word tied to what happened.
branches.cn: 报道、真实与语气三者，都把这个词拴在「发生过的事」上。

intro.en: Factual is built on fact with the adjective suffix -ual; fact itself comes from Latin factum.
intro.cn: factual 由 fact 加形容词后缀 -ual 构成；fact 本身来自拉丁语 factum。

latinIntro.en: Latin factum means a thing done, from facere, to do; the suffix -ual descends from Latin -alis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 factum 意为所做之事，源于 facere（做）；后缀 -ual 源自拉丁语 -alis。

items.example: Factum is the direct source of fact.
items.exampleCN: factum 是 fact 的直接来源。
后缀 -alis 变为英语的 -al 或 -ual。

items.meaning: a thing known to be true
items.example: Fact keeps the sense of something done.
items.exampleCN: fact 保留「做过之事」的意思。

items.meaning: relating to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 能力；官能；院系；全体教员
definition_en: a natural ability or power of mind or body; a department of a university; all the teachers of a university or school
core_image: 一个人身上可以被调用的几项本领，也是一所大学里的几大学院
scene: 她在语言方面很有天赋。She has a great faculty for languages.
sceneCN: 这里 faculty 是「能力、天赋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在语言方面很有天赋。

senses.title: A natural ability
senses.definition: a natural ability or power of the mind or body
senses.definitionCN: 心智或身体天生具备的能力
senses.example: He has a faculty for solving puzzles.
senses.exampleCN: 他有解谜的天赋。
senses.why: The base sense is an inner power that can be used.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是可以被调用的内在能力。

senses.title: A university department
senses.definition: a division of a university that groups related subjects
senses.definitionCN: 大学中按相关学科划分的部门
senses.example: She teaches in the faculty of law.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法学院任教。
senses.why: A group of scholars forms a body with its own powers.
senses.whyCN: 一群学者组成拥有自身权能的团体。

senses.title: The teaching staff
senses.definition: all the teachers and researchers of a university or school
senses.definitionCN: 一所大学或学校的全体教师与研究人员
senses.example: The faculty voted for the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 全体教员投票支持新规定。
senses.why: The department sense extends to the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 院系义延伸到其中的成员。

senses.title: An academic staff member
senses.definition: a member of the teaching or research staff at a university, especially in American English
senses.definitionCN: 大学的教师或研究人员，尤用于美式英语
senses.example: Two faculty attended the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 两名教职员出席了典礼。
senses.why: American usage treats the group word as a count noun for members.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语把这个集合名词用作可数的成员。

intro.en: Faculty comes from Latin facultas, ability or opportunity, from facilis.
intro.cn: faculty 来自拉丁语 facultas（能力、机会），源头是 facilis。

items.en: Facultas means ability or opportunity.
items.cn: facultas 意为能力或机会。

items.en: Facilis means easy to do.
items.cn: facilis 意为容易做的。

items.en: Faculte names a power or branch of learning.
items.cn: faculte 指一种能力或学问分支。

items.en: The word names a division of study.
items.cn: 中世纪大学用该词指学科分部。

items.en: Faculty also means the teaching staff.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faculty 也指全体教员。

note.en: Faculty is an ability or academic body; facility is a place or ease.
note.cn: faculty 是能力或院系，facility 则是设施或便利。

entries.definition: a place or equipment for a purpose
not working correctly
based on facts
the power to do something
a division of an organization
the people who work for an organization

normalIntro.en: Faculty moves from inner powers to the academic body that uses them.
normalIntro.cn: faculty 从内在能力延伸到运用这些能力的学术团体。

normal.en: She has a faculty for making people laugh.
normal.cn: 她有逗人发笑的本事。

normal.en: The faculty of medicine is highly ranked.
normal.cn: 医学院排名很高。

normal.en: The faculty met to discuss the curriculum.
normal.cn: 全体教员开会讨论课程。

normal.en: He lost his mental faculties after the illness.
normal.cn: 病后他丧失了心智能力。

normal.en: Every faculty member received a copy.
normal.cn: 每位教职员都收到了一份。

abstract.en: Picture several switches inside a mind, each a skill.
abstract.cn: 想象头脑里有几个开关，每个对应一种本领。

abstract.en: Imagine a university building named after an ability.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋以能力命名的大学建筑。

abstract.en: Think of teachers gathered as one powerful body.
abstract.cn: 把教师们想成凝聚成的一个有力整体。

examples.en: The faculty of speech develops early in children.
examples.cn: 语言能力在儿童早期发展。

examples.en: She joined the faculty of the university.
examples.cn: 她加入了这所大学的教职。

examples.en: The faculty approved the new programme.
examples.cn: 全体教员批准了新课程。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: faculty 与 facility 同源，都来自「容易、能做」；能做某事的能力，就是 faculty。

root: faculty 源自拉丁语 facultas（能力、机会），来自 facilis（容易的），由「做得到」引申为能力与院系。

sensesIntro.en: Faculty is a natural ability, a university division, the teaching staff, or one of its members.
sensesIntro.cn: faculty 指天生能力、大学院系、全体教员，或其中一位教职员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inner powers grouped into a learned body.
core.cn: 核心意象：内在能力聚合成一个学术团体。

branches.en: The base sense is an inner ability.
branches.cn: 基础义是内在能力。

branches.en: Scholars group into a department.
branches.cn: 学者组成院系。

branches.en: The group body means all teachers.
branches.cn: 这一团体指全体教师。

branches.en: American usage counts individual members.
branches.cn: 美式用法把成员视作可数个体。

branches.en: A faculty is both a division and its people.
branches.cn: faculty 既是院系也是其中的人。

intro.en: Faculty shares the Latin root of facility and facile.
intro.cn: faculty 与 facility、facile 共用拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin facultas and facilis explain faculty and its related forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facultas 与 facilis 解释了 faculty 及其相关形式。

items.example: Each faculty member has an office.
items.exampleCN: 每位教职员都有办公室。

items.meaning: a meeting of the teaching staff
items.example: The faculty meeting starts at noon.

items.meaning: the law department of a university
items.example: He studies at the faculty of law.
Old age can weaken mental faculties.
items.exampleCN: 年老可能削弱心智官能。

items.example: Ask your faculty adviser for help.

latinEntries.exampleCN: facilis 演变为 facility 与 facile。

definition_zh: 褪色；逐渐消失；减弱；衰退
definition_en: to lose colour or brightness; to become gradually weaker or quieter until it disappears; to decline in strength or importance
core_image: 阳光把布料的颜色一点点晒淡，直到几乎看不见
scene: 窗帘被太阳晒得褪色了。The curtains faded in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 fade 是「褪色」（第 1 个义项）；句意：窗帘被太阳晒得褪色了。

senses.title: To lose colour
senses.definition: to lose colour or brightness over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间失去颜色或光泽
senses.example: The curtains faded in the strong sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘在强烈的阳光下褪色了。
senses.why: The core sense is colour slowly leaving a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是颜色慢慢从表面退去。

senses.title: To become weaker
senses.definition: to become gradually weaker, quieter, or less clear until it disappears
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐变弱、变轻或变模糊直至消失
senses.example: The music faded as the train left.
senses.exampleCN: 火车开走时音乐声渐渐消失。
senses.why: Sound and light fade in the same soft way as colour.
senses.whyCN: 声音与光线像颜色一样柔和地消退。

senses.title: To decline
senses.definition: to lose strength, importance, or energy
senses.definitionCN: 失去力量、重要性或活力
senses.example: His hopes of winning faded over the season.
senses.exampleCN: 他夺冠的希望随着赛季推进逐渐破灭。
senses.why: The image of fading colour extends to abstract strength.
senses.whyCN: 褪色的意象延伸到抽象的力量。

intro.en: Fade comes from Old French fade, pale, probably from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: fade 来自古法语 fade（苍白的），可能源于日耳曼词根。

items.en: Fade means pale or dull.
items.cn: fade 意为苍白的、暗淡的。

items.en: The verb means to lose colour.
items.cn: 中古英语中该动词意为失去颜色。

items.en: Fade also describes light growing weak.
items.cn: 十六世纪 fade 也描述光线变弱。

items.en: Fade describes sounds dying away.
items.cn: 十九世纪 fade 描述声音渐逝。

items.en: Fade in and fade out name film transitions.
items.cn: 现代英语用 fade in 与 fade out 指影视转场。

note.en: Fade means to grow faint; fate is what is destined to happen.
note.cn: fade 是逐渐变淡，fate 则是命运。

entries.definition: the power that decides events
not genuine
the front of the head
to become or make less bright
to become smaller or weaker
to disappear completely

normalIntro.en: Fade is the slow loss of colour, sound, or strength.
normalIntro.cn: fade 是颜色、声音或力量的缓慢流失。

normal.en: The old photographs have faded.
normal.cn: 这些旧照片已经褪色了。

normal.en: Her voice faded into silence.
normal.cn: 她的声音渐渐归于寂静。

normal.en: The memory of that day faded.
normal.cn: 那天的记忆渐渐淡去。

normal.en: The music faded out at the end.
normal.cn: 音乐在结尾处淡出。

normal.en: His enthusiasm faded after a few weeks.
normal.cn: 几周后他的热情消退了。

abstract.en: Picture a bright shirt left for years in the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一件鲜艳衬衫在阳光下晒了多年。

abstract.en: Imagine a sound walking slowly out of hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象声音慢慢走出听觉范围。

abstract.en: Think of a hope growing thinner like mist.
abstract.cn: 把希望想成越来越薄的雾。

examples.en: The blue paint had faded to grey.
examples.cn: 蓝色油漆已经褪成了灰色。

examples.en: The applause faded as the curtain fell.
examples.cn: 幕布落下时掌声渐渐平息。

examples.en: Her anger faded when she heard the truth.
examples.cn: 她听到真相后怒意消退了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fade 原意是「苍白、暗淡」，颜色、声音、记忆由浓转淡的过程都是 fade。

root: fade 来自古法语 fade（苍白的、暗淡的），可能源于日耳曼词根，本义与「失去鲜明」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Fade means to lose colour, to grow weaker, or to decline.
sensesIntro.cn: fade 意为褪色、逐渐变弱或衰退。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: colour and sound slowly thinning away.
core.cn: 核心意象：颜色与声音慢慢变淡。

branches.en: The base sense is losing colour.
branches.cn: 基础义是失去颜色。

branches.en: Light and sound grow weak in the same way.
branches.cn: 光线与声音以同样方式变弱。

branches.en: Abstract strength also declines.
branches.cn: 抽象的力量同样会衰退。

branches.en: Both are gradual losses of intensity.
branches.cn: 两者都是强度的逐渐流失。

branches.en: What fades may vanish or simply weaken.
branches.cn: 消退之物可能消失，也可能只是变弱。

intro.en: Fade is a short verb that builds adjectives and phrasal verbs.
intro.cn: fade 是一个短动词，能构成形容词与短语动词。

latinIntro.en: Fade has no Latin root; its history is French and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: fade 没有拉丁词根，其历史属于法语与日耳曼语。

items.exampleCN: 他穿着一件褪色的夹克。

items.example: The fading light warned us to go home.
items.exampleCN: 渐暗的光线提醒我们该回家了。

items.example: She kept an unfading memory of him.
items.exampleCN: 她对他保持着不褪色的记忆。
他们使用了抗褪色的油漆。

definition_zh: 华氏温标；华氏的
definition_en: a temperature scale on which water freezes at thirty two degrees and boils at two hundred twelve
core_image: 温度计上刻着两套刻度，一套常见于英美天气预报，另一套是摄氏度
scene: 天气预报说今天华氏九十度，换算过来差不多是三十二摄氏度。The forecast gave ninety degrees Fahrenheit, which is about thirty two Celsius.
sceneCN: 这里指「华氏温标」（第 1 个义项：以华氏命名的一种温度标度）；句意：天气预报说华氏九十度，约合三十二摄氏度。

senses.title: The scale
senses.definition: the temperature scale named after Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit
senses.definitionCN: 以丹尼尔·加布里埃尔·华伦海特命名的温标
senses.example: The thermometer shows sixty eight degrees Fahrenheit.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示华氏六十八度。
senses.why: The scale carries the name of the instrument maker who proposed it in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 这一标度沿用了十八世纪提出它的仪器制造者的姓氏。

senses.title: The unit of difference
senses.definition: a temperature interval one hundred and eighty times the interval between freezing and boiling water
senses.definitionCN: 把水的冰点到沸点分成一百八十份后的一份间隔
senses.example: A rise of nine degrees Fahrenheit equals five degrees Celsius.
senses.exampleCN: 华氏升高九度相当于摄氏升高五度。
senses.why: Because the two fixed points are divided differently, a Fahrenheit degree is not the same size as a Celsius degree.
senses.whyCN: 两种标度把两个定点分成的份数不同，所以一华氏度与一摄氏度并不等长。

senses.title: Attributive use
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark a reading on that scale
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，标明该读数属于华氏标度
senses.example: A Fahrenheit reading of one hundred is very hot.
senses.exampleCN: 华氏一百度的读数非常热。
senses.why: English often turns a scale name into an adjective without changing its form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把标度名直接当形容词用，词形不变。

intro.en: Fahrenheit is an eponym: the scale takes the surname of its inventor.
intro.cn: fahrenheit 是姓氏命名词：标度取自发明者的姓。

items.en: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit builds precision thermometers.
items.cn: 丹尼尔·加布里埃尔·华伦海特制造精密温度计。

items.en: He fixes two reference points and divides the range.
items.cn: 他定下两个参考点并把区间分份。

items.en: English writers adopt his name for the scale.
items.cn: 英语作者用他的姓来称呼这种标度。

items.en: The word becomes a common noun and adjective.
items.cn: 这个词变成普通名词与形容词。

items.en: It survives mainly in United States weather reports.
items.cn: 它主要保留在美国的天气报道里。

note.en: Fahrenheit belongs to the family of temperature scale names.
note.cn: fahrenheit 属于温度标度名这一族。

entries.definition: just or pleasant
a small magical being
quite or justly
the scale freezing at zero and boiling at one hundred
the scale starting at absolute zero
an instrument for measuring temperature

normalIntro.en: A surname became a scale: Fahrenheit named the degrees he fixed.
normalIntro.cn: 一个姓变成了标度：华伦海特给自定的度数命了名。

normal.en: Water freezes at thirty two degrees Fahrenheit.
normal.cn: 水在华氏三十二度结冰。

normal.en: The report gave the temperature in Fahrenheit.
normal.cn: 报道用华氏给出了气温。

normal.en: Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit by multiplying and adding.
normal.cn: 把摄氏换算成华氏要先乘再加。

normal.en: A Fahrenheit degree is smaller than a Celsius degree.
normal.cn: 一华氏度比一摄氏度小。

normal.en: Compare Celsius: the same idea with a different inventor.
normal.cn: 对比 celsius：同样的思路，不同的发明者。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer with two scales printed side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计上并排印着两套刻度。

abstract.en: Imagine a workshop where a craftsman etches his own marks.
abstract.cn: 想象作坊里工匠刻下自己的刻度。

abstract.en: Think of a weather map using the older scale out of habit.
abstract.cn: 想象一张出于习惯仍在用旧标度的天气图。

examples.en: The oven was set to four hundred degrees Fahrenheit.
examples.cn: 烤箱设定在华氏四百度。

examples.en: Please convert thirty Celsius into Fahrenheit.
examples.cn: 请把摄氏三十度换算成华氏。

examples.en: Fahrenheit readings are still common in American forecasts.
examples.cn: 美国的天气预报仍常用华氏读数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「华伦海特」的姓直接成了标度名——记人名，就记住了这个词；只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 德语姓氏 Fahrenheit（华伦海特）→ 英语 fahrenheit（华氏温标），核心义「以发明者命名的温度刻度」。

sensesIntro.en: Fahrenheit first names the scale, then the size of one degree, then its attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: fahrenheit 先指标度，再指一度的间隔，最后指定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer carrying a craftsman name on its scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计的刻度上带着工匠的姓。

branches.en: The scale name is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 标度名是日常义项。

branches.en: The degree size is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 度的间隔是技术义项。

branches.en: The adjective use keeps the same form.
branches.cn: 形容词用法词形不变。

branches.en: A scale and its unit always travel together.
branches.cn: 标度与单位总是同时出现。

branches.en: Name and modifier are the same word.
branches.cn: 名称与修饰语是同一个词。

intro.en: Fahrenheit is an eponym rather than a Latin derivative, but scale words connect it to a family.
intro.cn: fahrenheit 是姓氏命名词，不是拉丁派生，但标度词把它连成一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies gradus, a step, which underlies degree and gradient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradus（步、阶）支撑 degree 与 gradient。

items.example: The surname is the whole source.
The word keeps the surname spelling.

items.exampleCN: thermometer 由 thermos 与 metron 组成。

items.example: Scale comes from scala, a ladder.
Celsius follows the same naming pattern.
items.exampleCN: celsius 遵循同样的命名方式。
kelvin 同样是姓氏命名词。

definition_zh: 失败；失败的人或事；故障；未做到
definition_en: a lack of success; a person or thing that is unsuccessful; a breakdown in a machine or system; the fact of not doing something required
core_image: 一场努力最终没有抵达终点
scene: 停电使机器全部停止运转。The power failure stopped all the machines.
sceneCN: 这里 failure 是「故障」（第 3 个义项）；句意：停电使机器全部停止运转。

senses.title: A lack of success
senses.definition: a lack of success in achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 在达成某事上缺乏成功
senses.example: The project ended in failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目以失败告终。
senses.why: The base sense is the general state of not succeeding.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是未能成功的总体状态。

senses.title: An unsuccessful person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that is unsuccessful
senses.definitionCN: 不成功的人或事物
senses.example: The film was a complete failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影彻底失败了。
senses.why: The abstract state becomes a countable instance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象状态变成可数的具体例子。

senses.title: A breakdown
senses.definition: a breakdown in a machine, system, or organ
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或器官的故障
senses.example: A power failure closed the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 一次停电让机场关闭。
senses.why: A thing that cannot work has failed its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 无法工作的东西就是未能履行职责。

senses.title: An omission
senses.definition: the fact of not doing something that is required
senses.definitionCN: 没有做被要求做的事情
senses.example: His failure to reply annoyed them.
senses.exampleCN: 他未回复让他们很恼火。
senses.why: Not doing a duty is a failure to meet it.
senses.whyCN: 未履行义务就是未能达到要求。

intro.en: Failure comes from Anglo-French failer plus the noun ending -ure.
intro.cn: failure 由盎格鲁-法语 failer 加名词后缀 -ure 构成。

items.en: Fallere means to deceive or disappoint.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗或使人失望。

items.en: Faillir means to miss or lack.
items.cn: faillir 意为错过或欠缺。

items.en: Failer becomes the legal verb form.
items.cn: failer 成为法律语境中的动词形式。

items.en: Failure names the state of falling short.
items.cn: 十七世纪 failure 指未达标的状况。

items.en: Failure also names machine breakdowns.
items.cn: 现代英语中 failure 也指机器故障。

note.en: Failure is the result; fail is the action.
note.cn: failure 是结果，fail 则是动作。

entries.definition: to not succeed
an important part or quality
a fixed piece of equipment
the state of losing a contest
a failure of a machine or system
a complete failure

normalIntro.en: Failure is the noun for every kind of fail.
normalIntro.cn: failure 是各种 fail 的名词形式。

normal.en: Failure is often the first step to success.
normal.cn: 失败常常是成功的第一步。

normal.en: The experiment was a failure.
normal.cn: 这次实验失败了。

normal.en: A power failure darkened the city.
normal.cn: 一次停电让城市陷入黑暗。

normal.en: His failure to appear worried us.
normal.cn: 他没有出现让我们担心。

normal.en: The failure rate of the device is low.
normal.cn: 这个设备的故障率很低。

abstract.en: Picture a rocket falling back to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭落回地面。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge that never reaches the far bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一座始终到不了对岸的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp suddenly going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯突然熄灭。

examples.en: He learned more from failure than from success.
examples.cn: 他从失败中学到的比从成功中学到的更多。

examples.en: The engine failure forced an emergency landing.
examples.cn: 引擎故障迫使飞机紧急降落。

examples.en: Her failure to sign the form caused a delay.
examples.cn: 她未在表格上签字造成了延误。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 动词变名词
dict_mnemonic.text: fail（失败）+ -ure（名词后缀）= failure（失败），与 nature、pressure 的构词方式相同。

root: failure 由 fail（失败）加名词后缀 -ure 构成，最终源自拉丁语 fallere（使人失望）。

sensesIntro.en: Failure is lack of success, an unsuccessful thing, a breakdown, or an omission.
sensesIntro.cn: failure 指不成功、失败的人或事、故障，或未做到某事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an effort that never reaches its goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：始终没有抵达目标的努力。

branches.en: The base sense is lack of success.
branches.cn: 基础义是缺乏成功。

branches.en: The state becomes a countable failure.
branches.cn: 状态变成可数的失败实例。

branches.en: A machine failure is a breakdown.
branches.cn: 机器 failure 就是故障。

branches.en: Failure to act is an omission.
branches.cn: 未行动就是一种疏忽。

branches.en: Broken systems and broken plans share the word.
branches.cn: 坏掉的系统与落空的计划共用一词。

intro.en: The suffix -ure turns the verb fail into a noun of result.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ure 把动词 fail 变成表示结果的名词。

latinIntro.en: Failure traces through French to Latin fallere, to deceive.
latinIntro.cn: failure 经由法语追溯到拉丁语 fallere（欺骗）。

items.meaning: lack of success or a breakdown

items.exampleCN: 她始终如一的善意帮助了我们。

items.meaning: safe even if a part fails
items.example: The reactor has a fail-safe design.
items.exampleCN: 反应堆采用故障安全设计。

items.meaning: the heart's inability to pump properly
items.exampleCN: 心力衰竭需要谨慎治疗。

items.example: The power failure lasted an hour.
The failure rate fell after the fix.

latinEntries.example: Fallere is the source of fail and false.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fallere 是 fail 与 false 的源头。

definition_zh: 昏倒；晕倒；微弱的；模糊的；虚弱的
definition_en: to lose consciousness for a short time; weak and not clear to see or hear; feeling weak and dizzy; slight and not strong
core_image: 眼前的光和声音一起变淡，人慢慢失去知觉
scene: 她因饥饿晕倒了。She fainted from hunger.
sceneCN: 这里 faint 是「昏倒、晕倒」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她因饥饿晕倒了。

senses.title: To lose consciousness
senses.definition: to lose consciousness for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 短暂失去知觉
senses.example: He fainted in the hot room.
senses.exampleCN: 他在闷热的房间里晕倒了。
senses.why: The verb sense is the body switching off briefly.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是身体短暂「关机」。

senses.title: Weak and unclear
senses.definition: weak and not clear to see, hear, or smell
senses.definitionCN: 视觉、听觉或嗅觉上微弱而不清晰
senses.example: A faint light showed under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门底下透出微弱的光。
senses.why: The weak signal is like consciousness almost gone.
senses.whyCN: 微弱信号就像意识几乎消失。

senses.title: Feeling weak
senses.definition: feeling weak and dizzy, as if about to faint
senses.definitionCN: 感到虚弱头晕，仿佛快要昏倒
senses.example: She felt faint after standing up quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 她猛地站起来后感到眩晕。
senses.why: The body approaches the state of fainting.
senses.whyCN: 身体正处于接近昏倒的状态。

senses.title: Slight
senses.definition: slight and not strong or likely
senses.definitionCN: 轻微、不强或可能性不大
senses.example: There is a faint hope that he will return.
senses.exampleCN: 他回来的希望很渺茫。
senses.why: A weak signal becomes a small chance or trace.
senses.whyCN: 微弱信号引申为渺小机会或痕迹。

intro.en: Faint comes from Old French feint, sluggish or pretended, from feindre, to feign.
intro.cn: faint 来自古法语 feint（无力的、假装的），源头 feindre（假装）。

items.en: Fingere means to shape or pretend.
items.cn: fingere 意为塑造或假装。

items.en: Feindre means to pretend or hesitate.
items.cn: feindre 意为假装或迟疑。

items.en: Faint means weak or weary.
items.cn: 中古英语中 faint 意为虚弱或疲惫。

items.en: The verb means to lose consciousness.
items.cn: 现代英语中动词义为失去知觉。

items.en: Faint also describes weak signals and slight chances.
items.cn: 当代英语中 faint 也描述微弱信号与渺小机会。

note.en: Faint means weak; feint is a deceptive move.
note.cn: faint 是虚弱的，feint 则是佯攻。

entries.definition: a movement meant to deceive
coloured liquid for surfaces
a very holy person
to lose consciousness
not bright or clear
not strong

normalIntro.en: Faint describes both the body going dark and signals growing weak.
normalIntro.cn: faint 既描述身体失去知觉，也描述信号变弱。

normal.en: She felt faint in the heat.
normal.cn: 她在高温中感到头晕。

normal.en: He fainted at the sight of blood.
normal.cn: 他一见血就晕倒了。

normal.en: A faint smell of smoke filled the room.
normal.cn: 房间里弥漫着淡淡的烟味。

normal.en: We heard a faint sound in the distance.
normal.cn: 我们听到远处有微弱的声音。

normal.en: There is a faint chance of rain.
normal.cn: 下雨的可能性很小。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned down to its lowest glow.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被调到最暗的光。

abstract.en: Imagine the room tilting as your knees give way.
abstract.cn: 想象膝盖发软、房间倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a hope as thin as a thread of smoke.
abstract.cn: 把希望想成细如烟丝。

examples.en: The hiker fainted from the heat.
examples.cn: 徒步者因高温晕倒了。

examples.en: There was a faint outline of a ship on the horizon.
examples.cn: 地平线上有一艘船的模糊轮廓。

examples.en: She gave a faint smile and left.
examples.cn: 她淡淡一笑便离开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: faint 原意是「无力的」，力气从身体退去会昏倒，光与声从感官退去就变得 faint。

root: faint 来自古法语 feint（无力的、假装的），源自拉丁语 fingere（塑造、假装），由「无力」引申出昏倒与微弱。

sensesIntro.en: Faint means to lose consciousness, or to be weak, unclear, dizzy, or slight.
sensesIntro.cn: faint 意为昏倒，或表示微弱、模糊、眩晕、轻微。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: senses dimming until the body switches off.
core.cn: 核心意象：感官变暗直到身体关机。

branches.en: The verb sense is losing consciousness.
branches.cn: 动词义是失去知觉。

branches.en: Signals become weak and unclear.
branches.cn: 信号变得微弱模糊。

branches.en: The body feels close to fainting.
branches.cn: 身体感到接近昏倒。

branches.en: Weakness becomes a slight chance or trace.
branches.cn: 微弱引申为渺小机会或痕迹。

branches.en: Feeling faint is the warning before fainting.
branches.cn: 眩晕是昏倒前的预警。

intro.en: Faint builds adverbs and nouns with -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: faint 通过 -ly 与 -ness 构成副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: Faint traces back through French to Latin fingere, to shape or pretend.
latinIntro.cn: faint 经由法语追溯到拉丁语 fingere（塑造、假装）。

items.meaning: to pass out or to be weak

items.example: He faints at the sight of blood.
Fainting can signal low blood pressure.
I do not have the faintest idea.
This task is not for the fainthearted.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务不适合胆小的人。

latinEntries.example: Fingere is the distant root of faint.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fingere 是 faint 的远源。

definition_zh: 公平的；白皙的；合理的；集市；博览会
definition_en: treating people equally and according to the rules; light in colour; reasonable and acceptable; a market or exhibition
core_image: 天平两端放得一样平，谁也不多占一点
scene: 裁判必须公平对待双方。The referee must be fair to both sides.
sceneCN: 这里 fair 是「公平的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：裁判必须公平对待双方。

senses.title: Treating people equally
senses.definition: treating people equally and according to the rules
senses.definitionCN: 一视同仁并按规定行事
senses.example: The judge was fair to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 法官对每个人都公正。
senses.why: The core sense is balance between competing sides.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是竞争双方之间的平衡。

senses.title: Light in colour
senses.definition: light in colour, especially hair or skin
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浅，尤指头发或皮肤
senses.example: The child has fair hair.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子有一头浅色头发。
senses.why: The old sense of beautiful or bright survives in colour.
senses.whyCN: 古老「美丽、明亮」之义残留在颜色上。

senses.title: Reasonable
senses.definition: reasonable and acceptable, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 合理可接受，虽不算出色
senses.example: We paid a fair price for the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我们以合理的价格买了这辆车。
senses.why: A balanced deal is a fair deal.
senses.whyCN: 平衡的交易就是公平交易。

senses.title: A market or exhibition
senses.definition: a public event with stalls, amusements, or goods for sale
senses.definitionCN: 设有摊位、游乐设施或商品出售的公共活动
senses.example: The village fair opens every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的集市每年春天开市。
senses.why: The noun comes from a separate Latin word for a holiday.
senses.whyCN: 该名词来自另一个表示节日的拉丁词。

intro.en: Fair as an adjective comes from Old English fæger; the market sense comes from Latin feria, a holiday.
intro.cn: 形容词 fair 来自古英语 fæger；集市义则来自拉丁语 feria（节日）。

items.en: Fæger means beautiful or pleasant.
items.cn: fæger 意为美丽的、宜人的。

items.en: Fair develops the sense of just and equal.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fair 发展出公正平等之义。

items.en: Feria means a festival day.
items.cn: feria 意为节日。

items.en: Feire names a market or festival.
items.cn: feire 指集市或节庆。

items.en: Trade fair keeps the market sense alive.
items.cn: trade fair 使集市义延续至今。

note.en: Fair means just or light; fare is the price of a journey.
note.cn: fair 是公平或浅色，fare 则是车费。

entries.definition: the money paid for a journey
a natural talent
strong belief or trust
morally right and fair
light in colour
fair and sensible

normalIntro.en: Fair covers justice, light colour, a reasonable deal, and a lively market.
normalIntro.cn: fair 涵盖公正、浅色、合理交易与热闹集市。

normal.en: Everyone deserves a fair trial.
normal.cn: 每个人都应得到公正的审判。

normal.en: The rules must be fair to all players.
normal.cn: 规则必须对所有选手公平。

normal.en: She has fair skin and dark eyes.
normal.cn: 她皮肤白皙，眼睛乌黑。

normal.en: That is a fair question.
normal.cn: 这是个合理的问题。

normal.en: We visited the book fair on Sunday.
normal.cn: 我们周日去了书展。

abstract.en: Picture a scale perfectly level on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架两边完全水平的天平。

abstract.en: Imagine sunlight falling on pale hair.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光照在浅色头发上。

abstract.en: Think of a field full of colourful stalls.
abstract.cn: 想象满是彩色摊位的场地。

examples.en: It is not fair to blame her.
examples.cn: 责怪她是不公平的。

examples.en: They agreed on a fair price.
examples.cn: 他们商定了一个合理的价格。

examples.en: The science fair attracted many students.
examples.cn: 科学展吸引了许多学生。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 双源同形
dict_mnemonic.text: 形容词 fair（公平、浅色）是英语本族词；名词 fair（集市）来自拉丁语 feria（节日），两义同形不同源。

root: 形容词 fair 源自古英语 fæger（美丽的、宜人的），引申为公正与浅色；集市义另来自拉丁语 feria（节日）。

sensesIntro.en: Fair means just, light in colour, reasonable, or a market.
sensesIntro.cn: fair 意为公正、浅色、合理，或集市博览会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with equal weight on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：两端等重的天平。

branches.en: The base sense is equal treatment.
branches.cn: 基础义是平等对待。

branches.en: Brightness survives as light colour.
branches.cn: 明亮义留存为浅色。

branches.en: A balanced deal is reasonable.
branches.cn: 平衡的交易就是合理的。

branches.en: The market sense comes from another root.
branches.cn: 集市义来自另一词根。

branches.en: Justice and fair prices share one balance.
branches.cn: 公正与公道的价格共享同一种平衡。

intro.en: Fair builds fairness and fairly, and pairs with un- for unfair.
intro.cn: fair 构成 fairness 与 fairly，并与 un- 组合成 unfair。

latinIntro.en: The market sense comes from Latin feria, but the adjective is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 集市义来自拉丁语 feria，但形容词义属日耳曼语。

items.meaning: just, pale, reasonable, or a market

items.example: She was the fairest in the tale.
The trade fair opens on Monday.
Fair play is the spirit of the game.
items.exampleCN: 公平竞争是这项运动的精神。

latinEntries.example: Feria gives the market sense of fair.
latinEntries.exampleCN: feria 给出 fair 的集市义。

definition_zh: 相当地；公平地；正当地
definition_en: to a moderate degree, quite; in a just and equal way; in a way that is deserved or according to the rules
core_image: 把强度调到中等，也把天平摆平
scene: 这部电影相当有趣。The film is fairly interesting.
sceneCN: 这里 fairly 是「相当地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这部电影相当有趣。

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: to a moderate degree, more than a little but not very
senses.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，不止一点但不算很
senses.example: The test was fairly easy.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考试相当容易。
senses.why: The base sense here is a moderate level.
senses.whyCN: 此基础义是中等水平。

senses.title: In a just way
senses.definition: in a way that treats people equally and honestly
senses.definitionCN: 以平等诚实对待他人的方式
senses.example: The workers were treated fairly.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们受到了公平对待。
senses.why: The adverb applies the justice sense of fair.
senses.whyCN: 该副词落实 fair 的公正义。

senses.title: By right
senses.definition: in a way that is deserved or allowed by the rules
senses.definitionCN: 以应得或符合规则的方式
senses.example: They fairly earned their place in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 他们凭实力正当地进入了决赛。
senses.why: A fair result is one that is deserved.
senses.whyCN: 公平的结果就是应得的结果。

intro.en: Fairly is fair plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: fairly 由 fair 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Fæger means beautiful or pleasant.
items.cn: fæger 意为美丽的、宜人的。

items.en: Fair gains the sense of just.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fair 获得公正之义。

items.en: Fairly means in a just manner.
items.cn: 十六世纪 fairly 意为以公正方式。

items.en: Fairly develops the sense of quite.
items.cn: 十九世纪 fairly 发展出「相当」之义。

items.en: Fairly often softens an opinion.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fairly 常用来缓和评价。

note.en: Fairly means quite; fairy means a magical being.
note.cn: fairly 是相当地，fairy 则是仙女。

entries.definition: just or light in colour
a small magical being
parents and children
to a moderate or large degree
in a fair way
in a fair and sensible way

normalIntro.en: Fairly can soften a word or make it just.
normalIntro.cn: fairly 既能缓和语气，也能表达公正。

normal.en: The room was fairly clean.
normal.cn: 房间相当干净。

normal.en: I am fairly sure she will agree.
normal.cn: 我相当确定她会同意。

normal.en: The staff treated us fairly.
normal.cn: 工作人员公平地对待我们。

normal.en: The match was fairly played.
normal.cn: 这场比赛公平进行。

normal.en: He fairly deserved the award.
normal.cn: 他完全配得上这个奖。

abstract.en: Picture a dial set halfway, not high or low.
abstract.cn: 想象旋钮停在中间，不高也不低。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale kept level by an honest hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只诚实的手让天平保持水平。

abstract.en: Think of a prize that was earned, not given.
abstract.cn: 想象一个挣来的、而非白给的奖。

examples.en: The instructions are fairly simple.
examples.cn: 说明相当简单。

examples.en: Every complaint should be fairly examined.
examples.cn: 每一起投诉都应得到公平审查。

examples.en: She fairly won the race.
examples.cn: 她正当地赢得了比赛。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 后缀派生
dict_mnemonic.text: fair（公平的）+ -ly（副词后缀）= fairly，既可表「公平地」，也可表「相当地」。

root: fairly 由 fair（公平的、合理的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，源自古英语 fæger。

sensesIntro.en: Fairly means to a moderate degree, justly, or deservedly.
sensesIntro.cn: fairly 意为相当地、公平地，或正当地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level scale and a middle setting on a dial.
core.cn: 核心意象：水平的天平与居中的旋钮。

branches.en: The base sense here is a moderate degree.
branches.cn: 此基础义是中等程度。

branches.en: The word applies justice to an action.
branches.cn: 该词把公正用于行动。

branches.en: A fair result is a deserved one.
branches.cn: 公平的结果就是应得的结果。

branches.en: Both reduce force: one in degree, one in judgment.
branches.cn: 两者都降低力度：一个在程度，一个在评判。

branches.en: Just treatment and fair reward go together.
branches.cn: 公正对待与公平回报相伴。

intro.en: The suffix -ly turns fair into an adverb with two main senses.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ly 把 fair 变成具有两个主要义项的副词。

latinIntro.en: Fairly has a Germanic root; only the market noun has Latin origin.
latinIntro.cn: fairly 属日耳曼词根，只有集市名词义源自拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 我们想要一个公平的决定。
有人提出了更公平的制度。
他们寻求最公平的解决方案。

items.example: We are fairly certain of the date.

latinEntries.example: Feria is unrelated to the adjective fair.
latinEntries.exampleCN: feria 与形容词 fair 无关。
